explanation: Archive-only rationale (unverified). The baseline BFS planner already reported success on all ten recorded learning-scope tasks, so no failure is observed in the available evidence; the baseline's main structural weakness is that its search space is global (men positions x carried spanner x nut/location facts), which scales poorly. The submitted revision keeps the same public contract, domain semantics, and output format, and replaces global state-space search with a goal-directed constructive procedure: BFS on the static directed link graph for walking routes, then, per still-loose goal nut, walk the man, fetch a useable spanner (one tightening consumes one spanner), tighten, and continue. This removes the exponential state expansion while preserving preconditions (at man loc, at nut loc, carrying spanner, useable, loose) and effects exactly as declared. It is not claimed to be optimal nor to generalize beyond the recorded scope; it is a bounded-risk simplification that keeps the ten observed successes intact for the goal patterns seen (tighten all nuts in a linear location graph).
